cards.title: Earth is actually closest to the Sun during the Northern Hemisphere's winter
cards.body: Many assume summer arrives because Earth swings closer to the Sun in its elliptical orbit. In reality, Earth reaches its closest point to the Sun, perihelion, in early January. Seasons are driven instead by Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt. When a hemisphere leans toward the Sun, daylight lasts longer and sunlight strikes the ground more directly, concentrating solar energy and heating the surface far more efficiently.

cards.title: Lactic acid is not what leaves your muscles sore days after a workout
cards.body: Delayed-onset muscle soreness, or DOMS, often strikes one to two days after intense exercise, leading many to blame pooled lactic acid. In truth, your body clears lactate within roughly an hour of finishing physical exertion. The lingering soreness is actually caused by microscopic tears in muscle fibers and the subsequent immune inflammation that repairs, rebuilds, and strengthens those tissues.

cards.title: The chemical that can set sand, concrete, and asbestos on fire
cards.body: Chlorine trifluoride is one of the most aggressively reactive chemical compounds ever synthesized. Because it acts as an oxidizer even more powerful than pure oxygen, it can ignite substances normally used to extinguish fires. Exposure to this pale greenish gas causes sand, bricks, concrete, and even wet asbestos to burst spontaneously into flame without an ignition source. It also reacts violently with water, exploding on contact.

cards.title: Deep space cosmic rays make radiocarbon dating possible
cards.body: Radiocarbon dating relies on continuous bombardment from deep space. High-energy cosmic rays collide with nitrogen atoms in the upper atmosphere, transmuting them into radioactive carbon-14. Living organisms absorb this isotope through photosynthesis and food in equilibrium with the atmosphere. When an organism dies, intake halts and the trapped carbon-14 decays with a predictable half-life of 5,730 years, giving archaeologists a natural molecular clock accurate up to 50,000 years.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1960 - Willard F. Libby

cards.title: A brainless single-celled organism can design efficient rail networks
cards.body: The yellow slime mold Physarum polycephalum lacks a brain, neurons, or sensory organs, yet it demonstrates astonishing decentralized problem-solving. In a famous experiment, researchers placed oat flakes on a map corresponding to major population hubs around Tokyo. The organism deployed nutrient-carrying tubes to connect the food sources. Within hours, it formed a resilient, low-cost transport network that nearly mirrored the real-world engineering of Tokyo's acclaimed subway system.

sources.title: Rules for Biologically Inspired Adaptive Network Design

quizzes.question: What is the primary physical cause of Earth's seasonal changes?
options: Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt
The varying distance between Earth and the Sun
Cyclic changes in the Sun's magnetic activity
Seasonal fluctuations in atmospheric greenhouse gases
quizzes.explanation: Seasons are driven by Earth's axial tilt, which changes the angle and concentration of sunlight hitting each hemisphere throughout the year.

quizzes.question: What actually causes the muscle soreness felt one to two days after a workout?
options: Microscopic muscle tears and inflammatory repair
Lactic acid crystal accumulation in joints
Dehydration within the tendon sheaths
Complete depletion of cellular ATP reserves
quizzes.explanation: Lactic acid clears within an hour after exercise; delayed soreness stems from microscopic tissue tears and the inflammatory healing response.

quizzes.question: Why can chlorine trifluoride ignite materials normally considered fireproof, such as sand and concrete?
options: It acts as a far more aggressive oxidizer than oxygen
It undergoes spontaneous nuclear fission on contact
It dissolves chemical bonds through ultra-high acidity
It produces intense sonic shockwaves upon contact
quizzes.explanation: Chlorine trifluoride is an oxidizer so potent that it forcibly reacts with substances that are already fully oxidized, like sand and concrete.

quizzes.question: Which atmospheric element is transformed into carbon-14 by cosmic rays from space?
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Argon
Hydrogen
quizzes.explanation: Cosmic ray neutrons collide with nitrogen-14 nuclei in the upper atmosphere, knocking out a proton to produce carbon-14.

quizzes.question: Which complex infrastructure layout did the brainless slime mold Physarum polycephalum replicate using oat flakes?
options: Tokyo's regional railway system
The Roman aqueduct network
The Panama Canal locks
London's subterranean sewage routes
quizzes.explanation: Physarum polycephalum optimized its feeding tubes into a layout remarkably similar in efficiency and resilience to the Tokyo rail network.

guesses.prompt: By how many degrees is Earth's rotational axis tilted relative to its orbital plane?
guesses.explanation: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt dictates how sunlight strikes the surface, creating the cycle of seasons.

guesses.prompt: What is the half-life of radioactive carbon-14 used in archaeological dating?
guesses.explanation: Carbon-14 decays with a half-life of 5,730 years, enabling dating of organic remains up to roughly 50,000 years old.

misconceptions.claim: Summer occurs because Earth moves closer to the Sun in its orbit.
misconceptions.explanation: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January; seasons are governed entirely by axial tilt, not orbital distance.

misconceptions.claim: Muscle soreness felt two days after exercising is caused by lingering lactic acid.
misconceptions.explanation: Lactate is flushed within about an hour; delayed-onset soreness comes from microscopic muscle tears and repair inflammation.

misconceptions.claim: Normally fireproof materials like concrete and asbestos can spontaneously ignite under certain chemical exposures.
misconceptions.explanation: Exposure to chlorine trifluoride, an oxidizer stronger than oxygen, causes sand, concrete, and asbestos to burst into flame.

misconceptions.claim: Optimizing complex transit networks requires an organism with a centralized brain and nervous system.
misconceptions.explanation: The single-celled slime mold Physarum polycephalum successfully replicates efficient transit maps through decentralized biological feedback.
